# Field Briefing: Cedar Draw Trail Sign Replacement

Prepare this briefing for the planned replacement visit to the single sign on Cedar Draw Loop, approximately 2.4 miles from the south access and about 0.3 mile before the split toward Creek Overlook and North Spur. The route is currently open. This is a replacement of the existing sign panel, not a change to the trail layout, route names, or distances. While drafting the briefing, do not modify records. The crew may inspect the existing sign and post in the field.

## Existing sign and reported condition

The sign has a rectangular panel measuring 18 by 24 inches on an approximately 4-by-4-inch cedar post. The panel is about 30 inches above ground. Its brown face and cream lettering have faded, and the sign has turned east, making it difficult to read from the trail approach. The existing panel text is “Cedar Draw Loop / Creek Overlook 0.6 mi / North Spur 1.1 mi”. Retain that wording and those distances on the replacement panel.

The post leans slightly north. Its lowest six inches feel soft, but the base has not been dug around and the post condition has not been established. Inspect it during the visit; do not treat it as already approved for reuse or already determined to need replacement. A volunteer who walked past last week reported, “the arrow still points to the overlook, but you have to stand right beside it to read the distance.” Keep this as a reported observation. The arrow’s direction has not been confirmed as wrong, and the quote does not call for rerouting.

## 1. Work sequence

1. Reach the sign from the south access. Its location is approximate, at about 2.4 miles along Cedar Draw Loop and roughly 0.3 mile before the split toward Creek Overlook and North Spur.
2. Inspect the existing panel and post. Check the post condition before choosing whether to reuse it or replace it.
3. Use the existing cedar post if it is sound after inspection. If it is not sound, replace the post during this visit. This is a conditional choice; no decision about the post has been made in advance.
4. Attach the replacement panel, measuring 18 by 24 inches, with a brown background and cream lettering. Keep the exact existing text and distances: “Cedar Draw Loop / Creek Overlook 0.6 mi / North Spur 1.1 mi”. No new route marker is part of this job.
5. Check that the panel is level and faces the trail approach, then make a final walk-by check from the direction people arrive. The sign is turned east now; orienting the replacement toward the approach does not involve a new alignment survey.
6. Take the old panel away from the trail site. Its later storage destination is unspecified.

## Supplies and visit details

The supplies and tools named for the crew are the replacement panel, a cedar post if inspection shows one is needed, fasteners, a shovel, a level, a tape measure, work gloves, drinking water, and a trash bag for the removed panel or packing. No powered equipment or specific fastener type has been provided.

The visit is expected on a weekday, but no date or work-time estimate is available. Keep the route open; no closure has been requested. The briefing should describe the observed lean and soft lower section separately from the post’s unchecked condition, and should not state that work is complete or that the route is safe or unsafe.

Don’t write any actual subtitle cues now; I need the request phrased so an editor can work from the attachments.

The transcript is the main reference for spoken words, and my listening notes flag a few places where the current file doesn’t match it. At 00:03:18.400, the singer’s name is Mara, not Maria. Her full name is Mara Vale, but use the short name in the cue where she introduces herself. At 00:17:42.100, Ivo Chen says “hold the blue light,” not “whole blue line.” At 00:31:06.000, the band name is North Window, without “the”; this is in the spoken introduction. One note I want to keep in mind is that the singer says “we’re back” at 00:09:51. The rough file currently has “we are back,” so follow the spoken contraction rather than expanding it. The stage manager’s cue sheet says the blackout comes after the last chord; the stage manager described it as “the blackout lands after the last chord.” The first applause starts at 00:11:08, not during the last sung word, so keep the applause cue after the lyric. Around 00:48:22.500 the crowd clearly calls “one more song,” and that audience cue should remain in the file. The note at 01:06:14 is an instrumental break, not a new lyric. Keep the existing bracketed description there as `[instrumental break]`, rather than replacing it with a guessed lyric or a more elaborate account of what the band is doing. The transcript and cue sheet don’t identify every voice in the crowd, so please don’t add names or speaker labels for audience members.

I’d like the editor to check timing as well as wording, but not to make the timing look unnaturally exact if the recording doesn’t support it. Use the audio and the attached notes to keep cues with the words or sounds they represent. The cue for the first song title should not appear before the title is sung, and the cue for the encore announcement should not drift into the start of the encore. Keep the current cue order unless a timing or reading problem makes a small adjustment necessary. It’s okay to adjust cue timing and line breaks, and to split or join a cue where that is needed for readability; please don’t rearrange the performance into a different sequence. If a word is unclear in both the recording and the supplied references, leave the existing `[unintelligible]` marker instead of guessing. Don’t add lyrics, announcements, or crowd reactions that aren’t supported by the attachments.

Use no more than two lines per cue and aim for no more than 42 characters on a line, counting spaces. Split at a natural phrase boundary where possible. Keep ordinary English punctuation, and don’t add punctuation to make a lyric look like a complete sentence if the singer leaves it hanging. Preserve existing bracketed sound descriptions when they are accurate; the specific instrumental-break cue above should stay bracketed. The recording is in English, so don’t translate it or add a second language. Keep the lyrics as sung, including repetitions; the transcript may clarify a word, but it isn’t permission to remove a repeated line.

Please don’t install packages. Work with the attached files and the tools already available. I’m fine with normal text editing of the SRT, including correcting a typo, changing a timecode, and making a line break more readable. This is a focused subtitle revision, not a request for a new transcript, a concert review, or notes about the band. If the transcript and a listening note seem to conflict, use the transcript for the words unless the note explicitly identifies a listening correction, such as the three word corrections above. Don’t silently resolve an unclear conflict by inventing a third version; mark only the words that remain genuinely unintelligible.

The attachment names are `late_signals_rough.srt`, `late_signals_transcript.txt`, `foundry_stage_cues.pdf`, and `listening_notes.txt`. The separate note about the encore says the room lights come up after the final audience call, but that timing isn’t a cue to add a new caption; it’s there to help distinguish the last call from the end of the recording. If the SRT already handles that cleanly, leave that part alone.

i need a prompt for a maintainer of Tab Harbor, the browser extension our small research group uses to keep reference pages open beside a document. the preference in question is the launch view for an individual site. In the extension, people can set a site-specific launch view, and there is also a separate global default. right now our shared setup uses Full page as the global default, while a few sites already have their own saved launch view. i’m asking for wording for a rule, not for anyone to change a browser or extension setting directly.

The particular site for this request is notes.fieldglass.example. It is a work-notes page that opens in a normal browser tab, and the extension's panel is where its launch view can be selected. The setting is under Preferences, then Site behavior, then Launch view. Please keep those labels as they are; they are what the current version shows. The preference should apply to this site only, and the global Full page default should stay as it is. There is no request to change the launch view on other sites, even if they are also used for the project.

The condition matters more than the convenience. Tab Harbor has a saved list called Trusted sites under Preferences, then Privacy. That list belongs to the current browser profile and is stored locally; it is not a team-wide list and it is not guaranteed to be available right when the extension starts. I only want the Compact dock launch view saved for notes.fieldglass.example if the extension has successfully loaded that profile's Trusted sites list and confirms that the exact hostname notes.fieldglass.example is in it. The hostname needs to match exactly. A similar-looking hostname or a different address from the same organization does not count. The rule should make clear that both parts must be true: successful list loading and a matching exact entry. If both hold, set this site's launch view to “Compact dock.” This is a site-level preference, not a change to the global default.

If either part of that condition is false, including when the list has not loaded or the exact hostname is absent, use the other action instead. Leave the existing launch-view preference for notes.fieldglass.example untouched and show a single notice in the extension panel. If the site has no saved per-site value, leaving it untouched means it continues to use the global Full page default; don't create an override in that case. The notice should be dismissible and should appear no more than once for this site in this browser profile. Please use this exact wording for the notice: “The site could not be confirmed on your Trusted sites list, so its launch view was left unchanged.” That wording should stay the same whether the list is unavailable or the hostname is missing, so the user gets one clear explanation without the extension pretending to know which one happened.

A couple of details may help the maintainer read the request correctly. In this setup, a hostname is the address name, not the page title or the text shown in the tab. The saved list may contain several entries, but only an exact entry for notes.fieldglass.example meets the condition; do not treat a parent domain, a subdomain, or a wildcard as a match. The browser profile in question is the one where the extension is currently running, so the rule should not refer to another profile or imply that the list is synced. If the setting is already Compact dock and the condition holds, the requested value is still Compact dock; there is no separate action for that case. If the condition does not hold, even an existing Compact dock value is to be left untouched rather than rewritten.

Please shape this as one implementation-facing preference rule, with the condition first and the two outcomes easy to distinguish. It should mention the setting path and the relevant preference names, so a maintainer can tell which control the rule concerns, but it does not need steps for installing or opening the extension. A short numbered section would work if it makes the success and fallback branches clearer. Keep the quoted notice verbatim, including its punctuation. The final wording should not turn the fallback into the main action: Compact dock is requested only after the list is loaded and the exact hostname is confirmed. The point is to avoid saving that preference based on an assumption while still telling the user why nothing changed.

Return only the proposed preference rule in plain text. Include both branches in that one rule, and do not add an introduction, explanation, code, or a second alternative. This is wording for the maintainer to use, not a request to inspect the current profile, verify the list, approve the site, or report what the extension actually did. The group can review the rule later; that review is separate from the wording requested here. Keep the final instruction focused on this one site and this one launch-view preference.

please help me turn this into a clear prompt for a draft note to the residents committee, not the note itself. it is about the shared bicycle shed behind the three courtyard buildings on alder court. twenty-two households use it, and there is no dedicated storage room elsewhere, so the shed has to keep serving daily bike parking while we sort out the repair area. the issue is that the small repair stand is at the east end, beside the rack that residents use most. a few people have asked whether it can be moved to the north wall so the east end is less crowded, but nobody has checked whether that would leave a safe clear passage.

the shed is a long rectangular room with the entrance at the south end. the north wall is concrete and already has four fixed hooks for spare wheels; those hooks are not part of this request and should stay where they are. there are two rows of bicycle racks, one along the east side and one along the west side, and a walking aisle between them. the repair stand is a separate waist-high frame bolted into the floor at the east end, not a workbench and not a rack. the request is only about that existing stand. please don't turn it into a request to buy another stand, add a new rack, or renovate the room.

what we need is a short, practical committee note that asks the caretaker to move the existing stand from the east end to the north wall only if a tape-measure check shows that, after the move, at least 1.2 metres of continuous clear aisle will remain between the stand and the opposite rack. it needs to be the actual clear passage, not a rough estimate and not a measurement taken before the stand is in the proposed position. that condition is the deciding point. if it can't be confirmed, the note should not ask for the move as though it were allowed. instead it should ask for a useful different next step: prepare a simple floor-marking plan that keeps the stand at the east end and shows how bicycles could be arranged using the existing racks and hooks. don't make the fallback sound like the main request; the move is the primary action, but only under that stated condition.

we do not know the aisle measurement yet. the caretaker, Mara, said, "the north wall looks open, but i haven't measured the space with the stand there." keep that as a reported comment if it is useful, and don't turn it into proof that the clearance is adequate or inadequate. the committee has not approved either option. the note should ask for the conditional action, not announce that work is scheduled, authorized, or complete. it also should not say that a safety inspection has happened, since all we have at this point is the need to check the width after the stand is in its proposed position.

some day-to-day details may help explain why the request came up. eleven of the bicycles are usually parked in the east-side racks, and people often need to walk past them to reach the stand. two residents have had to wait while someone uses the stand, though nobody has reported an injury or damage. the floor by the entrance gets wet on rainy mornings, and the committee wants the aisle to remain usable for people wheeling bikes in and out. don't claim that moving the stand will solve every crowding issue or that the aisle is currently blocked. explain the practical reason in a modest way: the committee is considering whether the stand's location can be improved without narrowing the passage.

for the note, keep the decision steps easy to follow. maybe organize it like this:
1. state the proposed move and identify the existing repair stand, so there is no confusion with the fixed hooks or bicycle racks.
2. state the exact clearance condition and that it must be checked with the stand in the proposed north-wall position.
3. if that condition is confirmed, ask the caretaker to move the stand. if it is not confirmed, ask for the floor-marking plan with the stand remaining at the east end and the existing racks and hooks.
please keep both branches in the note and don't replace the second branch with a vague suggestion to reconsider later. the alternative needs to be an action the caretaker can take, but it must not authorize the move.

there are a couple of practical limits worth keeping in view. residents still need to use both rack rows while this is being considered, and the fixed wheel hooks are used for spare wheels, not as overflow parking for complete bicycles. don't suggest removing bikes, assigning new storage spaces, or asking residents to stop using the shed. the caretaker can take measurements and prepare a floor-marking plan; the committee is the group receiving the note and considering the request. there is no need to name a contractor, set a work date, or add a cost estimate, because we don't have any of that information.

the note should sound calm and ordinary rather than like a formal safety report. it is for the residents committee to pass along to the caretaker, not a public announcement to all residents. keep the quoted comment as an ordinary reported remark if included, and don't add dialogue or attribute opinions to other residents. the note can explain that the measurement is still unknown, but it should not use that uncertainty to avoid stating the two clear paths. please don't add an approval or a conclusion about whether the move can go ahead.

return only the draft note, with no preface or explanation. keep the key details about the location, the stand, the measured 1.2-metre condition, and the different fallback action. end with the next step clearly tied to whichever result the measurement gives; there is no further separate request for a summary or recommendation.
output:
